body.title: Understanding is a pattern of behavior across new situations
body.text: I think understanding requires more than producing the right outputs. A system that only maps inputs to outputs can be correct without grasping why the answer is correct, as in Searle's argument about symbol manipulation. But that argument leans on an intuition about what grasping is, and the intuition may not survive a careful account of what human understanding consists of. My view is that the question should be rephrased: what behaviors would a system need to show across new situations for us to say it understands?
